newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: U.S. seen curbing Tamil rebels' fund-raising.
newsitem.headline: U.S. seen curbing Tamil rebels' fund-raising.

text.p: The United States is expected to help curb international fund-raising by Sri Lankan Tamil rebels fighting for independence, a cabinet minister said on Tuesday.
Justice and Constitutional Affairs Minister Gamini Lakshman Peiris told a news conference that U.S. State Department officials told him Washington would help Colombo fight terrorism.

Peiris, just back from a trip to Canada and the United States, said Washington was expected to include the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) on a list of terrorist groups being drawn up for completion probably by the end of this year.
"The (U.S.) officials who spoke to us were convinced that the LTTE would be one of the organisations that would appear on that list," he said.
"That, of course, will tremendously help Sri Lanka in combating international terrorism."
Peiris said once the United States branded the LTTE as a terrorist group, its bank assets would be frozen and its members deported and barred from entering the country.
Colombo has said it believes Tamil rebels finance their military activity through funds extorted from expatriate Sri Lankans in Western countries.
The Tamil Tigers are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east.

Many western nations condemned the LTTE for the bombing of Sri Lanka's central bank in January which killed nearly 100 people, and for the July bombing of a packed train in a suburb of Colombo in which 57 died.

"The focus (of the meetings) was very much on the question of fund-raising -- the raising of money in these countries -- and the ways in which these activities could be controlled by the authorities in these countries," he said.

Peiris, who led a Sri Lankan delegation, met senior state department officials, including Ambassador Philip Wilcox, the U.S. State Department's coordinator for counter-terrorism, and Assistant Secretary of State for South Asia Robin Raphel.
He also met visiting German Minister for Cooperation and Economic Development Carl Dieter Spranger in Washington, and Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy in Canada.
Wilcox said when he visited Colombo in August that Washington would stamp out illegal activities on U.S. soil directed against the Indian Ocean island's government.
Colombo has said more than 50,000 people have been killed in the ethnic war, now in its 14th year.
